name: The Ashfall Remembrance
description: On November 3, 2189, the Aurelius Corponation's atmospheric processing array in the northern MidRing malfunctioned catastrophically, releasing a plume of metallic particulate that settled over the Shelf's Ward 4 and Ward 6 districts for eleven days. Official records list 34 deaths; independent forensic collectives have documented over 900. Aurelius settled all claims quietly and the incident was reclassified as a 'controlled emissions event.' Every November 3rd, Shelf residents hang silver cloth from windows and balconies — a practice called 'the silver mourning' — and the streets go quiet for one hour at dusk.
cultural_impact: The Ashfall Remembrance is one of the few Shelf traditions that upper tiers actively pretend does not exist — Aurelius employs significant media suppression around the date, making it a litmus test for who in M88 actually controls information.
locations: Ward 6 'Silver Street' — informal name for Keswick Corridor
story_hooks: A player character is hired by Aurelius to locate and destroy the Groundcount Archive before the Remembrance, when attention on the incident peaks — but the archive is hosted inside a deceased Shelf elder's BCI ghost.
Someone has begun hanging silver cloth in Tier 3 neighborhoods, and Aurelius wants to know who is organizing the spread of the tradition upward before it reaches media visibility.
A Tier 4 Aurelius employee discovers their parent died in the Ashfall — and they never knew because the company altered their family's records.
origin_event: The 2189 Aurelius atmospheric array failure that released metallic particulate over Shelf Wards 4 and 6, causing mass casualties that were officially minimized and legally suppressed through closed settlements.
tier_observations: Tier 1 (Shelf): Silver cloth hung from every window in Ward 4 and 6; one hour of public silence at dusk; ghost markets close; handmade memorial tokens sold for Φ1-2; deeply felt. Tier 2: Some workers in Aurelius-adjacent sectors observe quietly at home, afraid of employment consequences; small acts of solidarity. Tier 3: Most are unaware due to media suppression; those who know keep it private. Tier 4-5: Effectively nonexistent; Aurelius employees receive an internal memo on the date reminding them of 'communications protocols' — which is itself an acknowledgment that the company fears the day.
